questions.q: Why would a developer store a discount threshold in a Custom Metadata Type instead of hardcoding it in Apex?
options: So an admin can adjust the business rule as data, and so changing it doesn't require a new code deployment
Apex cannot contain numeric literals
Custom Metadata Types run faster than literal values
Hardcoded values are not allowed by the Apex compiler
questions.explain: Storing configuration as metadata or settings data lets it be changed without a code deployment, and lets non-developers adjust it through the UI.

questions.q: What does the generated `getAll()` method return for a Custom Metadata Type?
options: A single record matching the first DeveloperName alphabetically
The total count of records as an Integer
A Map of every record for that type, keyed by DeveloperName
Nothing — getAll() is only available on Custom Settings, not Custom Metadata Types
questions.explain: getAll() returns every record of that Custom Metadata Type as a Map keyed by DeveloperName, mirroring the equivalent method on Custom Settings.

questions.q: Per Lesson 26's governor limits, what is true about querying Custom Metadata Type records?
options: It counts double against the SOQL query limit
It is only allowed in asynchronous Apex
It requires Database.query() and cannot use inline SOQL
It is exempt from the per-transaction SOQL query limit
questions.explain: Custom Metadata Type records are exempt from the SOQL query limit, making them safe to query freely from configuration-heavy code.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between Custom Metadata Type records and Custom Settings records?
options: There is no real difference; the two terms refer to the same feature
Custom Metadata Type records are metadata that moves with a deployment/package; Custom Settings data is regular org data that does not move that way
Custom Settings can only be read from Visualforce, never from Apex
Custom Metadata Types cannot have more than one field
questions.explain: Custom Metadata Type records travel with a package or deployment because they're metadata, while Custom Settings records are ordinary org data that has to be migrated or re-entered separately per environment.

questions.q: Why would a Hierarchy Custom Setting be a better fit than a Custom Metadata Type for a value that needs to vary per user?
options: Hierarchy Custom Settings are specifically designed to resolve to the most specific org/profile/user value automatically, which Custom Metadata Types don't natively support the same way
Custom Metadata Types cannot be read from Apex at all
Hierarchy Custom Settings are faster to query than Custom Metadata Types in every case
Custom Metadata Types can only store numeric fields
questions.explain: Hierarchy Custom Settings are purpose-built to resolve per org, profile, or user, with Apex automatically returning the most specific applicable value — a use case Custom Metadata Types don't natively cover.
